card: Disconnects sockets immediately when poll() reports error or hangup events on connections where reads were not requested, rather than attempting a doomed send or read first. This applies to both the P2P networking loop and the HTTP server, avoiding redundant failed I/O calls and clarifying debug log output upon disconnection. It also expands test coverage for TCP urgent data handling and peer resets during send stalls. Depends on PR #36716.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the full diff; the approach and scope are unchanged.
evidence: PR description: "`poll()` reports an error or hangup on a socket whether or not we asked for it. If that happens for a peer we did not request to read from, disconnect directly. This just adds clarity: previously we would attempt a send that would then fail. The only side-effect is a changed log message."

Commit cb18aedce8: "Disconnect directly on POLLERR/POLLHUP when no read was requested, skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect the peer. This also changes the debug log message."
problem: When `poll()` reports socket errors on an established connection where reads are paused (such as during backpressure or queued responses), the node proceeds to attempt a send or read that fails and triggers disconnection anyway. This causes redundant failed system calls and logs misleading errors instead of reporting the socket hangup directly.

risk.why: A logic error in socket event handling could prematurely disconnect healthy P2P peers or HTTP clients.

scope_notes: This PR includes commits from base PR #36716 that restrict the `select()` exception set to connection attempts.
summary: Handles socket error and hangup events in the P2P networking loop and HTTP server separately from socket read readiness. When `poll()` reports `POLLERR` or `POLLHUP` on a socket where reads are currently paused, the node disconnects immediately rather than attempting an outgoing send that is guaranteed to fail. It also adds unit and functional test coverage for TCP urgent (OOB) data handling and peer resets during send stalls.
